current_example.problem: The function $f(x) = e^{x-k}+2$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \ln{(x-2)}+4.$ What is the value of $k?$
current_example.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{x-k}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y-k}+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={e}^{y-k}+2 \\ {e}^{y-k} & =x-2 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y-k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2) \\ y-k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)+k\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is $f^{-1}(x) = \ln{(x-2)} + k.$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=4.$
